Only between.

Suppose a world begins with no named objects, just relationships that form and disappear. Will something persist long enough for us to call it a thing? We don't know. Change the rules and see what happens.

Network visualization. The statistics alongside describe the evolving structure.

Rules of this world

Initializing…

What would count as an object?

In this toy universe, an edge is a relationship. The points are anonymous positions in the network, not particles. A group is counted as a cluster when its points are connected by paths. A persistent cluster is a group with the same members surviving at least five successive steps. That's a definition we chose, not something nature supplied.

Each step, existing links may disappear; absent links may form spontaneously or become more likely when their endpoints share neighbors. The rules contain no instructions to create a particular shape, organism, or stable object. The initial links and subsequent choices are generated by a reproducible seeded random sequence.

Try setting shared-neighbor attraction to zero, then increasing it. Try increasing disappearance. Do structures become more persistent, or do they collapse into a single connected mass? Change the seed to test whether the behavior depends on one lucky starting arrangement.

Important limitations: A connected cluster is not automatically an independent object. The points, time steps, and update rules are predefined; the system is not literally made of relationships alone. This is an exploration of emergence, not evidence about quantum entanglement or the fundamental nature of our universe. No result is guaranteed.

All calculations run in this browser. Nothing is uploaded or tracked.
